tools.name: quantum_cloud_devices

tools.name: quantum_cloud_submit
tools.description: After human approval, submit a static OpenQASM 3 file inside the current workspace to a live UQC simulator. The adapter compiles the supported standard gates h, x, y, z, s, sdg, t, tdg, sx, sxdg, rz, p, u1, u2, u3, cx, cz and swap into the SDK basis rx, ry and rzz; native rx, ry and rzz are also accepted. Unsupported dynamic constructs or gates are rejected before network dispatch. measure and barrier are preserved; shots must be a multiple of 100 (100-1000). Accepts a file path, not a registered circuit_id: a user-created circuit does not require a runnable algorithm catalog entry. Never submits to hardware or returns circuit bodies. cloud_task is a remote receipt, not a company handle. Never retry automatically after an uncertain submission. Approval flows through the session's per-call ask channel at invocation time; make the tool call when the task warrants it and the channel handles the approval instead of waiting outside the session.

tools.name: quantum_cloud_status
tools.description: Query one UQC cloud task by its actual remote receipt. Returns a short state only, never bitstrings or full scientific results. The SDK has no task-history listing endpoint.

tools.name: quantum_cloud_result
tools.description: Reclaim a completed UQC simulator task result by its actual receipt as a bounded analysis summary: total shots and the at-most-eight most probable basis states as scientific-metrics probabilities. Full raw counts stay on the cloud platform web page; the platform SDK cannot cancel in-flight simulator tasks.

tools.name: hpc_queue

tools.name: hpc_submit

Approval flows through the session's per-call ask channel at invocation time; make the tool call when the task warrants it and the channel handles the approval instead of waiting outside the session.

script.description: Absolute POSIX path to a batch script that already exists on the authorized HPC gateway; default to a path under the per-account staging root from hpc_resources.staging_root (e.g. <staging_root>/demo.sh). Relative paths, ~ paths, Windows drive paths, spaces and inline script text are rejected. Verify the file first with hpc_script_check.

tools.name: hpc_job_status
tools.description: Reconcile one submitted SLURM job by number over the SSH gateway: live queue first, then accounting history. Returns one short row or an explicit not-found observation; never returns twin_id.

tools.name: hpc_script_check
tools.description: Read-only gateway probe: verify that one absolute POSIX script path already exists on the authorized HPC gateway before submitting. Returns the checked observation; never runs the script and never returns twin_id.

script.description: Absolute POSIX candidate script path on the authorized HPC gateway; default to the per-account staging root from hpc_resources.staging_root (e.g. <staging_root>/demo.sh); no ~, relative or Windows paths, no spaces.

tools.name: hpc_resources
tools.description: Read-only gateway probe: one short cluster inventory row per partition (node counts by state and core allocation/idle summary from sinfo), plus staging_root, the writable per-account staging directory derived from the SSH login account (always its home directory plus /company_agent). All upload, directory-create, submit and fetch paths default under staging_root; no job rows, no user quota claims, never returns twin_id.

staging_root.description: Writable per-account staging directory on the gateway, derived from the SSH login account's home directory (home + /company_agent); use it as the base for all upload, script, fetch and directory-create paths.

tools.name: hpc_file_list
tools.description: Read-only gateway probe: list regular files under one absolute POSIX directory on the authorized HPC gateway (depth one, at most 32 entries). Directories are not listed; no job rows; never returns twin_id.

path.description: Absolute POSIX directory on the authorized HPC gateway; default to the per-account staging root from hpc_resources.staging_root (e.g. <staging_root>); no ~, relative or Windows paths, no path traversal.

tools.name: hpc_file_fetch
tools.description: Read-only download: copy one regular UTF-8 text file (at most 48,000 bytes) from the authorized HPC gateway into the active DSH workspace under gateway/<basename>, and return only a bounded receipt (bytes and location). File content never enters the model context; never returns twin_id.

path.description: Absolute POSIX file path on the authorized HPC gateway under the per-account staging root from hpc_resources.staging_root (e.g. <staging_root>/slurm-5010.out); no ~, relative or Windows paths, no path traversal.

tools.name: hpc_stage_file

Requires human approval; refuses to touch an existing gateway file unless overwrite is true; never returns twin_id. Approval flows through the session's per-call ask channel at invocation time; make the tool call when the task warrants it and the channel handles the approval instead of waiting outside the session.

workspace_path.description: File inside the active DSH workspace, relative to the workspace root (e.g. jobs/demo.sh); no ~, no absolute paths, no traversal.

gateway_path.description: Absolute POSIX destination file path on the authorized HPC gateway inside the writable per-account staging root from hpc_resources.staging_root (e.g. <staging_root>/demo.sh); no ~, relative or Windows paths, no path traversal.

tools.name: hpc_job_cancel

tools.name: company_office_create
tools.description: Bounded single-file artifact creation inside a project directory of the mounted workspace (COMPANY_AGENT_TOOL_WORKSPACE), the write-side complement of company_office_analyze: writes .docx (WordprocessingML headings/paragraphs), .xlsx (multiple capped sheets), .xmind (XMind 8 content.xml package that WPS mind map and XMind open), .mm (FreeMind XML) and .txt/.md from a structured content object. Standard library only, atomic temp+replace write whose sha256 is re-verified by re-read; existing files refuse unless overwrite=true, cap overshoot (2000 blocks, 32 sheets, 5000 rows, 512 nodes, text budgets) refuses instead of truncating; no OCR, no conversion, no template execution, no external calls, no quantum handles.

project.description: Project directory inside the mounted workspace root; created on first write; must be a direct child directory of it.

path.description: Output file path relative to the project directory; must end in .docx, .xlsx, .xmind, .mm, .txt or .md; forward slashes only, no .. segments, no absolute paths.

content.description: Structured payload keyed by output kind: docx -> {blocks:[{kind:heading|paragraph,text:string,level:1..6}]}; xlsx -> {sheets:[{name:string,rows:[[{string|number|boolean|null}]]}]}; xmind/mm -> {root:{title:string,children:[node...]}}; txt/md -> {text:string}. The adapter validates each shape and refuses overshoot.

overwrite.description: Replace an existing file; absent/false refuses with an explicit error.

overwrote.description: True when overwrite replaced an existing file.

tools.name: company_office_analyze
tools.description: Read-only text ingestion for one file inside a project directory of the mounted workspace (COMPANY_AGENT_TOOL_WORKSPACE): docx paragraph text (paragraph-number anchors), xlsx per-sheet bounded previews (32 sheets, 5000 rows per sheet, explicit row omission), pptx per-slide text layers (32 slides, slide anchors), pdf text-layer pages (page anchors) and .txt/.md lines. 20MB file cap, result-budget paging via offset, always returns sha256/bytes and explicit truncated flags; legacy binaries (.doc/.xls/.ppt/.wps/.et/.dps), images and unknown suffixes fail closed honestly; no OCR, no conversion, no execution, no external calls, no quantum handles.

project.description: Project directory inside the mounted workspace root; must be a direct child directory of it.

path.description: File path relative to the project directory; forward slashes only, no .. segments, no absolute paths.

offset.description: Unit index to resume from: docx paragraph, xlsx sheet, pdf page or text line; independently 1-based item indexes are reported per item.

tools.name: company_office_compare
tools.description: Read-only line-level comparison for two same-kind files inside a project directory of the mounted workspace: .txt/.md lines or .docx visible paragraphs (the company_office_analyze L{n} anchors). Bounded to 4000 units per side: more refuses instead of comparing a stand-in; the receipt carries exact added/removed line counts, at most 40 hunk samples with an explicit truncated flag and 200 characters per shown line. Mixed kinds, unsupported kinds, non-UTF-8 text and corrupt packages fail closed; no conversion, no OCR, no external calls, no quantum handles.

project.description: Project directory inside the mounted workspace root; must be a direct child directory of it.

file_a.description: Workspace path relative to the project directory; forward slashes only, no .. segments, no absolute paths.

file_b.description: Workspace path relative to the project directory; forward slashes only, no .. segments, no absolute paths.

file_a.description: Workspace file path of side A as project/relative compound.

file_b.description: Workspace file path of side B as project/relative compound.

identical.description: True when both sides produce the same unit sequence.

added.description: Lines present in B and absent in A.

removed.description: Lines present in A and absent in B.

at_a.description: 1-based first A unit of the hunk, 0 when the hunk only adds.

at_b.description: 1-based first B unit of the hunk, 0 when the hunk only removes.

truncated.description: True when more than 40 hunks existed.

tools.name: company_office_edit
tools.description: Surgical tracked-changes editing for one existing .docx inside a project directory of the mounted workspace: each edit matches its find text inside a single paragraph's visible text, the before/after pair is reduced to minimal edit spans (common runs of 4+ characters stay untouched, no 6+ unchanged run inside a change), and the result lands as standard w:ins/w:del revisions with the given author and UTC date, so Word/WPS show Word-native accept/reject tracks. Anchors that miss are reported, anchors that hit more than once skip the whole edit unless occurrences=all, unchanged and newline-carrying finds/replace skip, and an edit batch that produces no tracked change refuses without writing anything. The written package is re-opened and the on-disk w:ins/w:del counts plus every changed paragraph's replayed visible text are re-verified before success (the B5 gate). Standard library only, atomic temp+replace write with sha256 re-verified by re-read, cap overshoot (128 edits, 4000 chars per find/replace) refuses; no conversion, no template execution, no external calls, no quantum handles.

project.description: Project directory inside the mounted workspace root; must be a direct child directory of it.

path.description: Existing .docx path relative to the project directory; any other suffix refuses. Revisions need an existing package: create one with company_office_create first.

find.description: Anchor text searched inside one paragraph's visible text; newlines are never part of it.

replace.description: Replacement text; empty means a tracked deletion. Newlines refuse.

occurrences.description: Absent: an anchor hitting more than once in the document skips this edit. Present as all: every hit in every paragraph becomes a tracked change.

author.description: Revision author written on every w:ins/w:del of this batch.

note.description: One-line reason for the audit ledger when COMPANY_AGENT_AUDIT_* is configured; missing ledger skips the line without changing the edit.

path.description: Workspace file path as project/relative compound.

tools.name: company_office_validate
tools.description: Evidence-anchor gate for one project directory of the mounted workspace: every reference carries a workspace file, a locator (L paragraph/line, P pdf page, S sheet!A1 cell) and the exact quote, and the tool re-reads the files and answers PASSED/FAILED/INCOMPLETE deterministically. Missing or mismatched fingerprints, missing files, unparsable locators and quote mismatches are FAILED; locators the bounded parsers do not implement (ranges such as S!A1:B2 and L ranges on structured kinds, non-text kinds) and empty quotes are INCOMPLETE, never a guess; PASSED only when every reference resolves. Docx paragraph anchors and pdf page anchors follow company_office_analyze numbering exactly. Bounded to 128 references, 128 source fingerprints, 4000 characters per quote; no external calls, no quantum handles.

project.description: Project directory inside the mounted workspace root; must be a direct child directory of it.

path.description: Workspace path relative to the project directory; forward slashes only, no .. segments, no absolute paths.

line_ref.description: L12, L12-L14, P3 or S quarterly!B4; anything else is an unparsable-locator issue.

quote.description: Visible text expected at the locator; empty is INCOMPLETE.

sources.description: Content fingerprints the references must match; a referenced path missing here is FAILED (fingerprint_missing).

path.description: Workspace path relative to the project directory; forward slashes only, no .. segments, no absolute paths.

code.description: fingerprint_missing | fingerprint_mismatch | file_missing | file_unreadable | locator_unparsable | locator_out_of_range | quote_mismatch | quote_empty | kind_unsupported

tools.name: company_office_chart
tools.description: Declarative chart artifact inside one project directory of the mounted workspace: bar/line/stacked_bar/pie specs render to a deterministic standalone SVG (same spec in, same bytes out) written next to the canonical spec JSON under artifacts/charts/<chart_id>.json and .svg, so the user reviews the semantic spec, not pixels. chart_id is the first 16 hex of the canonical spec digest. Standard library only, atomic temp+replace writes re-verified by re-read, existing files refuse without overwrite=true, cap overshoot (64 categories, 8 series, 64 values per series, series/category length mismatch, 800KB svg, pie with more than one series) refuses; no computation libraries, no network, no quantum handles.

project.description: Project directory inside the mounted workspace root; must be a direct child directory of it.

json_path.description: Canonical spec JSON path as project/relative compound.

svg_path.description: Deterministic SVG path as project/relative compound.

tools.name: company_office_matter
tools.description: Structured matter artifacts for one project directory of the mounted workspace, the industry-neutral port of the MeWork project extensions: kind=timeline writes the fixed file project.company-timeline.json (events with date/title/evidence), kind=chronology writes project.company-chronology.json (entries with date/fact/people/evidence), kind=mindmap writes project.company-mindmap.json (root, six layers, deeper subtrees truncate with an explicit issue). Upsert merges by id or by the date|title / date|fact key and keeps an existing anchored item when the incoming one has no evidence; replace must be passed explicitly for a full redo; an empty payload or an all-empty merge refuses to overwrite existing work. Dates accept 2026-03-01, 2026/3/1, 2026年3月1日, 2026-03, 2026年3月 and 2026年; unknown dates become issues and the item is dropped instead of guessed. Receipts count anchored versus unanchored items so missing evidence is named, not hidden. Standard library only, atomic write re-verified by re-read, cap overshoot (200 events/entries, 512 nodes, 4000 chars per text field) refuses; no external calls, no quantum handles.

tools.name: company_office_audit
tools.description: Read-only docx format audit inside one project directory of the mounted workspace, the L4 companion to surgical edits: mode=baseline checks one existing .docx against the GB/T 9704-2012 draft rule table (A4 page and 37/35/28/26mm margins, body 仿宋 16pt, first-line indent 2 chars, 26.5-30pt line band, title 小标宋 22pt centered, heading1 黑体 / heading2 楷体 / heading3 仿宋) and reports bounded issues with L{n} paragraph locators plus counts; mode=imported never applies the rule table - it describes the file's own dominant format as bounded facts and flags only structural anomalies such as several sections. What the bounded parser does not verify is listed in ``unchecked`` and never claimed as passing; the rule table is a replaceable draft pending the firm's confirmation. Bounded to 5000 checked paragraphs (more is truncated and honestly marked), 20MB file cap, 128 reported issues; page headers/tables/embedded fonts stay unchecked. Standard library only; no conversion, no fixing, no external calls, no quantum handles, nothing is written.

project.description: Project directory inside the mounted workspace root; must be a direct child directory of it.

path.description: Workspace path relative to the project directory pointing at an existing .docx; any other suffix refuses.

mode.description: baseline = audit against the GB/T 9704-2012 draft rule table (also the scope for an explicit full re-template request); imported = describe the file's own dominant format, no template applied.

path.description: Workspace file path as project/relative compound.

paragraphs_total.description: Every w:p of the body in document order, the company_office_analyze L{n} numbering.

truncated.description: True when more paragraphs existed than the checked cap; the tail is named in unchecked, never silently dropped.

status.description: Replaces the draft baseline once the firm confirms its own rule table.

facts.description: Observed format facts (margins, page size, dominant font/size/line spacing); the imported-mode deliverable.

source.description: Where the fact was read, e.g. sect or doc_defaults or L12.

locator.description: L12, L14 etc. for paragraph findings; sect / styles / document for structural ones.

unchecked.description: Items the bounded parser does not verify; honesty clause, not a pass.

tools.name: company_office_pptx
tools.description: Structured pptx generation and in-place shape text rewrite for one project directory of the mounted workspace, the stdlib port of the §4.5 slice (no officecli, no conversion): action=render writes one .pptx from a slide array where each slide is a structured layout - title (heading plus optional subtitle), agenda (numbered), bullets, two_column, matrix (a real PowerPoint table, up to 6x6 cells), checklist (checkbox-prefixed) - over named textboxes at fixed 16:9 geometry, so the deck opens in WPS/PowerPoint with page structure a human can edit rather than one full-page text box; action=edit rewrites the visible text of one shape per edit addressed as slide/shape (1-based document order of p:sp textboxes only, tables excluded) and refuses an edit batch entirely when any target is invalid - all-or-nothing, never a silent skip; every written package is re-opened and per-shape texts are replayed against what was built before the receipt returns (the B5 gate), and a failed edit verification restores the original bytes; action=preview is the §4.1 officecli visual path: it needs the binary resolved through COMPANY_AGENT_OFFICECLI or the adjacent search and honestly refuses when it is absent, then bounds one headless run (180s, 4MB stdout, minimal env) to per-page screenshots into preview/<stem>/ plus the editable shape enumeration. Caps are refusals, never stand-ins: 64 slides, 4000 characters per shape text (newlines refuse for edit), 8 bullets per column, 6x6 matrix cells; the written file reuses the P0 fences with atomic temp+replace, overwrite needs an explicit argument. Standard library only; no quantum handles.

action.description: render = generate the .pptx described by content; edit = rewrite visible text of existing shapes described by edits.

path.description: Workspace path relative to the project directory: render takes the .pptx to write (existing file refuses without overwrite), edit takes the existing .pptx to rewrite.

content.description: render payload: {slides:[{kind:title|agenda|bullets|two_column|matrix|checklist, title:string, subtitle?:string, bullets?:[string], left?:[string], right?:[string], matrix?:[[string]]}]}. The adapter validates each shape and refuses overshoot; agenda pairs 1..n prefixes, checklist prefixes a checkbox glyph, two_column needs left and right, matrix needs a rectangular 1..6 x 1..6 grid.

applied.description: render: 0. edit: number of edits whose replayed text matched. preview: 0.

screenshots.description: preview only: per-page PNG artifacts written under preview/<stem>/, page order 1..N.

tools.name: company_office_convert
tools.description: Local conversion inside one project directory of the mounted workspace, the L6 exit of the suite: .docx becomes a sibling .pdf and .doc becomes a sibling .docx through an explicitly configured headless LibreOffice (COMPANY_AGENT_SOFFICE, or soffice/libreoffice found on PATH); no engine found is a hard, honest failure - never a stand-in copy, nothing is uploaded anywhere. The converter holds a bounded lease so two tasks cannot fight over soffice; the child runs with a whitelisted environment, arrayed arguments and bounded stdout, and the produced file must pass the three-way check (exists, non-empty, right magic bytes and for docx an openable package with word/document.xml). Output naming stays next to the source as <stem>.<ext>, then <stem>_01.._99; overwriting the source is impossible by construction. 20MB input cap with honest refusal; no OCR, no template execution, no quantum handles.

tools.name: company_office_open
tools.description: Desktop exit for one workspace file, the §5.1 host integration ported to the Windows deployment: the file is opened with WPS through the current file association (registry-checked launcher must be WPS/Kingsoft, otherwise the call fails with a human message instead of silently falling back), or with the explicitly configured startfile mode when the operator prefers the system association. Launching requires COMPANY_AGENT_OPEN_WPS=wps|startfile to be set in the local environment - absent configuration is an honest refusal, not a surprise launch. Allowed kinds are bounded to office/pdf/text/old-binary suffixes; every launch (and every failure) carries an audit line when the ledger is configured. Bounded receipt: no machine paths beyond the workspace compound, launcher reduced to its basename. Standard library only.

project.description: Project directory inside the mounted workspace root; must be a direct child directory of it.

launcher.description: Executable basename actually launched; startfile reduces to 'shell'.

audited.description: True when the ledger line was written; audit config missing means false and the open still happened.

tools.name: company_office_compute
tools.description: Batch aggregation sandbox (the run_compute port) for ONE project directory of the mounted workspace: source code runs in a separate interpreter process with a curated builtin set and these whitelisted helpers only - list_files(pattern?), read_text(path), read_table(path .xlsx/.csv/.json/.txt/.md), stats(rows_or_column), write_text(path,text,overwrite?), write_table(rows,path,overwrite?,sheet_name?), emit_chart(spec,overwrite?), and a captured print. No imports, no getattr through dunders by convention, no network, no paths outside the project subtree; every read and write reuses the workspace fences, the write budget caps 200 files and 4MB per run, xlsx writes follow the spreadsheet caps, and the whole run stops at 30s or 80k source chars with an explicit refusal. The adapter re-verifies every written file by re-read and reports sha256. Requires the machine-level switch COMPANY_AGENT_COMPUTE_ALLOW=1: without it the call refuses honestly, keeping high-security deployments free of any code evaluation. Process isolation and curated namespaces are not an operating-system security boundary; that is a documented residual, and the switch is the control.

project.description: Project directory inside the mounted workspace root; must be a direct child directory of it; the compute sandbox sees exactly this subtree.

source.description: The batch program: whitelisted helpers + curated builtins; print(...) is captured.

result.description: Whatever the source assigned to RESULT (bounded 20KB JSON); empty object when absent.

charts.description: Chart artifact paths (json+svg pairs count once) the sandbox emitted.

sha256_writes.description: Re-read fingerprints of the written files in the same order as written.

tools.name: company_office_deliver
tools.description: Delivery naming for one workspace file (the MeWork present/named-deliverable port): the file is copied atomically into the project-level deliverables/ directory as <title>_<UTC YYYYMMDD>_<NN>.<ext>, where title defaults to the source stem (stripped of old date stamps like _20260101 or _20260101_02), NN is the next free two-digit sequence for that title and date, 1..99, and 99 breaks the tool honestly. The source file is never touched; an existing delivery name is never overwritten; the receipt carries project/relative paths only. Copy size cap 20MB. Standard library only.
